decisionMemo.businessProblem: A Series A SaaS company serving the construction industry is experiencing unexpected churn acceleration (4% Q2 → 6% Q3) while expansion ARR is declining relative to new customer acquisition. Unit economics appear healthy on paper (11-month LTV payback), but cohort-level data is still building. The company must understand whether churn is driven by (1) product fit issues (feature gap, usability), (2) customer fit issues (wrong customer segment acquired), (3) market dynamics (consolidation, customer acquisition pressure), or (4) pricing/economics issues (ROI story not resonating). Net revenue retention of 95% is unhealthy for SaaS; without expansion, the company is on a treadmill of constant acquisition to offset churn.
